findings.quote: it is densest at about $4\,^\circ\text{C}$ and gets less dense as it cools toward freezing, which is why ice floats.
findings.problem: Wrong cause, introduced by the round-1 fix. Ice floats because solid ice is less dense than liquid water: freezing lowers density by about 9 percent (USGS). The liquid's own drop in density between 4 and 0 degrees C is tiny (about 1.0000 to 0.9999 g/mL) and is not why ice floats; it explains why the coldest water stays on top and a lake freezes from the top down. The lesson never states that ice is less dense than liquid water, so a student asked why ice floats is led toward the true but wrong reason 'water is densest at 4 degrees C'.
findings.source: USGS Water Science School, 'Water Density' (accessed 2026-11-03): 'ice is less dense than liquid water, which causes it to float'; freezing lowers density by about 9 percent; checklist B01

findings.quote: The Moon pulls hardest on the water facing it. Water on the far side is pulled least.
findings.problem: This paragraph has six sentences, over the one-to-three limit. Others also run over: 'Surface currents are driven mainly by wind' paragraph (6), 'About $2.5\%$ of Earth's water is fresh water' (5), 'Density is how much mass fits' (5), 'The ocean forms layers' (5), and the first and third Speed Tricks paragraphs (5 each), plus several of four sentences.
